narrative.overview: Crema's landing page reads like a well-loved espresso bar after dark: warm bark and coffee-grounds darkness, a single cool Ink-navy accent that reads like the glow off a polished portafilter, and serif display type set big and confident like a chalkboard menu re-drawn in Iowan Old Style. It is not a SaaS-dashboard blue-and-white pitch deck; it is a real object in a real shop — a printed 4×6 recipe card literally rendered rotated and drop-shadowed on the page, grain and topo-line textures behind sections, a ticker of scrolling shop stats. The system rejects flat corporate minimalism and rejects the earlier gold accent in favor of a single, deliberately rare cool accent against a hot-toned dark ground.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, warm-toned ground (near-black coffee brown, not blue-black or pure gray)
One accent color (Ink navy) used sparingly and consistently for every interactive/emphasis moment
Serif display type for headlines/quotes; monospace for numbers/labels; system sans for body copy
Real printed-object imagery as a first-class UI element (the recipe card mockup)
Grain/topo/weave textures layered behind flat color for tactility

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Ink navy is the only color that means interactive or emphasis anywhere on the page. Ember, spruce, and alert are semantic and never substitute for the primary accent.

rules.name: The Light-Label-On-Dark-Fill Rule
rules.body: Any element filled solid with the Ink-navy fill token takes the on-crema (near-white) text color, never dark ink text.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for numbers and short data labels — never prose or headlines.

rules.name: The No-Elevation-In-Print Rule
rules.body: Every shadow, blur, and glass background reverts to flat white/ink at @media print.

dos: Do keep Ink navy as the only interactive/emphasis color.
Do pair any solid Ink-navy fill with on-crema (near-white) text.
Do use the serif for headlines/quotes/big numbers and mono for data-shaped content.
Do strip all shadows, blur, and dark backgrounds at @media print.
Do use the 999px pill radius for clickable elements and the 16px radius for containers.
donts: Don't reintroduce a warm/gold color as an interactive or primary-accent color.
Don't give a structural card a solid opaque background.
Don't add real photography as a background texture.
Don't use a soft ambient shadow on the recipe-card mockup.
